annotatedSteps.description: F1 and F2 percentages of violet flowers in Experiment 1 and reason
annotatedSteps.studentWork: A. Experiment one: F1 — 100% violet (Vv); F2 — 75% violet (VV and Vv), because violet is the dominant trait.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct percentages (100% in F1, 75% in F2) and valid reason.

annotatedSteps.description: F2 fraction/percentage of tall plants with white flowers in Experiment 2 and reason
annotatedSteps.studentWork: B. Tall plants with white flowers in F2 = 9/16, because tall is dominant.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Incorrect proportion. In a dihybrid cross (9:3:3:1 ratio), tall with white flowers is a recombinant phenotype with a probability of 3/16 (18.75%), not 9/16.
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Tall plants with white flowers in F2 = 3/16 (18.75%), as this is a recombinant combination resulting from independent assortment of genes.

annotatedSteps.description: F1 and F2 percentages of short plants with white flowers in Experiment 2 and reason
annotatedSteps.studentWork: D. F1: 0% short plants with white flowers, since all F1 plants (VvTt) show only the dominant traits. F2: 1/16 (6.25%) plants will be short with white flowers (vvtt), as both traits are recessive.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct percentages (0% in F1, 6.25% or 1/16 in F2) and clear reasoning.

teacherNote: Marked against: Part A: Percentage of violet flowers in F1 (100%) and F2 (75%) with valid reason (1.5); Part B: Expected percentage/fraction of tall plants with white flowers in F2 (3/16 or 18.75%) with reason (1); Part D: Expected percentage of short plants with white flowers in F1 (0%) and F2 (1/16 or 6.25%) with reason (1.5). Parts A and D are answered very clearly with accurate genetics reasoning. Be careful with dihybrid cross ratios in Part B: 9/16 represents individuals dominant for both traits (tall and violet), while tall with white flowers is 3/16.
